item.title: Reexamining and Replicating Foundational Studies in Entrepreneurship Research
item.content:encoded:
Karl Wennberg, Stockholm School of Economics

Jeremy C. Short, University of North Texas

Jeffrey A. Chandler, University of North Texas

Marcus Wolfe, University of North Texas

Sebastian Kruse, RWTH University

Carolin Krieweth, RWTH University

This special issue addresses a significant gap in entrepreneurship research by promoting rigorous replication studies of foundational empirical work. While replication is essential for cumulative theory development, entrepreneurship research currently lacks a strong replication culture. Many influential studies have never been replicated or replicated only once, leaving their robustness unexamined despite widespread influence on theoretical debates and practice.

The special issue welcomes theory-driven replication studies that revisit influential relationships and explore their boundary conditions and underlying mechanisms. Submissions may employ diverse methodologies, with emphasis on multi-study designs combining exact replication or reanalysis with subsequent empirical generalization. Replication is valued as a tool for theory refinement rather than mere confirmation, with assessment based on theoretical contribution and methodological rigor.

Appel publié par Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Replication studies in entrepreneurship
  • Foundational empirical studies
  • Robustness and boundary conditions of established relationships
  • Reanalysis of original data
  • Exact replication designs
  • Multi-study designs combining replication with generalization
  • Theoretical mechanisms and construct refinement
  • Most cited entrepreneurship studies
  • Methodological transparency and rigor in replication research
  • Context-specific patterns versus stable theoretical mechanisms
